news.title: Senator Imasuen hails Flamingos after World Cup win
news.lede: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen, has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos on their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, describing it as a landmark achievement for Nigeria and African football. Imasuen, who represents Edo South Senatorial District, praised the players for their resilience, determination and fighting spirit, which propelled them to become the first African nation to win the competition. In a congratulatory statement issued through his media aide, Moshood Karim, and made available to journalists in Abuja, the senator said the team’s journey from an opening-day defeat to six consecutive victories before lifting the trophy demonstrated their character, discipline and belief. The Flamingos made history on Saturday in Morocco after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final to claim the 2026 title.

news.title: Tinubu, NSC, NFF Hail Flamingos Over Historic FIFA U-17 World Cup Victory
news.lede: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the National Sports Commission (NSC) and the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) have congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos following their historic 2-1 victory over Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026. The victory, secured on Saturday in Rabat, made Nigeria the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, marking a major milestone for Nigerian football and women’s football on the continent. news.title: Flamingos set to arrive Nigeria after historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph
news.lede: November 8, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Nigerian News 0. Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, will return home from Morocco in the early hours of Monday, November 9, 2026 following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The team is scheduled to depart Morocco through the Mohammed V International Airport, Casablanca, at 1:00 a.m., with arrival expected at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at 5:00 a.m. The travel update was communicated by the team’s media officer, Erenayo Dorcas Koki, who also expressed appreciation to journalists and other media colleagues for their coverage and support throughout the tournament, blueprint reports.

news.title: Nigeria's Flamingos Make History by Winning FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria’s Flamingos have achieved what no African team had done before, winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. But as celebrations continue over the historic victory, attention is shifting to a bigger question: can Nigeria build on the success and ensure the players do not fade into obscurity after their moment of glory? The triumph has raised hopes for women’s football in the country, but stakeholders say the real test will be whether the Nigeria Football Federation and government invest in a system capable of producing and sustaining more world-class players.The Flamingos’ journey to the title was remarkable. They lost their opening match 2-1 to Poland but recovered to win six consecutive matches, defeating Puerto Rico, North Korea, Mexico, Venezuela, Brazil and Japan.

news.title: U17 Women’s World Cup: Akinwunmi hails Flamingos, attributes triumph to Tinubu ’s NSC sports reforms
news.lede: A former first Vice President of the Nigeria Football Federation, Seyi Akinwunmi, has commended Flamingos after they beat Japan in the final to become the first African country ever to lift FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup. Akinwunmi, a former Chairman of the Lagos State Football Association also gave credit to government. He hailed the reforms of the National Sports Commission (NSC), backed by the mandate of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “This victory did not happen by chance,” he said.

Japan head coach Sadayoshi Shirai has broken his silence after his side fell 2-1 to Nigeria's Flamingos in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, conceding that Nigeria's physical strength and speed were decisive factors in the outcome. The defeat made history as Nigeria became the first African nation to win the competition, completing one of the most dramatic runs the tournament has ever seen. Speaking to FIFA's official website after the final whistle, Shirai was candid about the challenge his players faced against the Flamingos.

news.title: Former NFF Official Credits Tinubu Administration for Flamingos' World Cup Victory
news.lede: Former Nigeria Football Federation First Vice-President, Seyi Akinwunmi, has described the Flamingos’ historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph as evidence of the benefits of sustained grassroots investment and the sports reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Akinwunmi, a former chairman of the Lagos State Football Association, spoke in Lagos after Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Morocco to become the first African nation to win the competition.
